newsitem.title: INDIA: India raises crude prices paid to ONGC.
newsitem.headline: India raises crude prices paid to ONGC.

text.p: The Indian government has raised the prices it pays to state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) for crude oil, ONGC said in a statement.
The statement, dated March 5, said the price increases, which are effective retroactively from April 1, 1996, "will have significant impact on profitability of ONGC".

"The government of India has officially communicated the enhancement of basic price and royalty of indigenous crude oil both onshore and offshore of ONGC with effect from April 1, 1996," the statement said.
The total price increase for crude oil is 300 rupees per tonne. Of this, 50 rupees will go towards royalty payment and 250 rupees will go to ONGC as retention price, the statement said.
The price of crude oil was last revised in April 1993. The revised price works out to about $7.50 per barrel against the existing international price of around $20 per barrel.

"This will have a significant impact on the profitability of ONGC and will also help ONGC in generating adequate international resources to meet out not only its outlay in India but will also help in promoting its business overseas", the statement said.
